subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 29-year-old woman is evaluated for an LDL cholesterol of 245 mg/dL and a normal triglyceride level. Her father had a myocardial infarction at age 43, and her brother has a similar lipid profile. Genetic testing shows normal LDL receptor expression but a variant that alters the receptor-binding region of the major LDL ligand.
question: Which of the following apolipoproteins is most likely defective in this patient?
explanation_correct: Apo B-100 is present on liver-derived VLDL, IDL, and LDL and is the ligand that binds the LDL receptor, permitting receptor-mediated endocytosis and LDL clearance. A variant that impairs this binding produces familial hypercholesterolemia with high LDL and premature atherosclerosis despite normal receptor expression. Apo B-48, in contrast, is made only in the intestine.

explanation_incorrect.A: Apo A-I is the LCAT activator on HDL and does not bind the LDL receptor.
explanation_incorrect.B: Apo C-II is a lipoprotein lipase cofactor acting on triglyceride-rich particles.
explanation_incorrect.C: Apo E mediates remnant uptake but is not the ligand that is defective in this patient's LDL particles.
explanation_incorrect.D: Apo B-48 is synthesized only in the small intestine and mediates chylomicron secretion.

educationalObjective: Apo B-100 is the LDL receptor ligand on liver-derived lipoproteins, and defective binding causes a dominantly inherited hypercholesterolemia phenotype.
